edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo. Simplicitas, bonitas, habitet in corpore vestro. Irasci nolite sine causa fratri devoto: Recipietis enim quidquid feceritis ab illo. Hoc placuit Christo, resurgere mortuos, imo, Cum suis corporibus, et quos ignis ussit in aevo, Sex millibus annis completis mundo finito. Vertitur interea coelum tenore mutato: Comburuntur enim impii tunc igne divino. Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo. Digniores, stemmate et generati praeclaro, Nobilesque viri sub Antichristo devicto: Ex praecepto Dei rursum viventes in aevo, Mille quidem annis ut serviant sanctis et Alto, Sub jugo servili, ut portent victualia collo; Ut iterum autem judicentur regno finito. Nullificantes Deum, completo millesimo anno, Ab igne peribunt, cum montibus ipsi loquendo. In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto, Demerguntur inferno, trahunt poenas in aevo. Ostenduntur illis, et legunt gesta de coelo Memoria prisca debito et merita digno. Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno. Omnia non possum comprehendere parvo libello. Curiositas docti inveniet nomen in isto.
pass_a_gloss: Future inhabitants of heaven with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Simplicity, goodness, let it dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother: For you will receive whatever you do from him. This pleased Christ, to resurrect the dead, indeed, with their bodies, and those whom fire has burned in the age, six thousand years completed the world ended. Meanwhile, the heaven is turned with a changed tenor: For the wicked are burned then by divine fire. The creature groans, burning with the anger of the highest God. More worthy, of noble lineage and born of illustrious, and noble men under Antichrist defeated: Living again by the command of God in the age, for a thousand years so that they may serve the saints and the Highest, under a servile yoke, so that they may carry provisions on their neck; So that they may be judged again with the kingdom ended. Those nullifying God, with the thousandth year completed, will perish from fire, with the mountains themselves speaking. All flesh is returned to pits and tombs, done, they are submerged in hell, they drag penalties in the age. These things are shown to them, and they read deeds from heaven, from ancient memory and due merit and worthy dignity. Reward in perpetuity according to deeds to the tyrant. I am not able to comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find a name in this.
pass_b_english: Future citizens of heaven will dwell with God Christ, who holds the first place and sees all things from heaven. Let simplicity and goodness make their home in your body. Do not be angry without cause at a devoted brother, for you will receive back from him whatever you have done. This pleased Christ: to raise the dead with their bodies, even those whom fire has consumed in the age, once six thousand years are complete and the world has ended. Meanwhile heaven itself is transformed, its order changed, for the wicked are then burned by divine fire. Creation groans, aflame with the anger of the Most High God. Men of nobler lineage and illustrious birth, noble men defeated under Antichrist, will live again in the age by God's command, for a thousand years, so that they may serve the saints and the Most High, beneath a slavish yoke, carrying provisions on their necks, and so that they may be judged once more when the kingdom ends. Those who nullify God, when the thousandth year is complete, will perish in fire, the very mountains speaking against them. All flesh is returned to pits and tombs, the deed done; they are plunged into hell and drag their penalties through the age. These things are shown to them, and they read the deeds recorded in heaven from ancient memory, with due merit and worthy dignity. Eternal reward goes to the tyrant according to his deeds. I cannot comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find a name in this.

review.notes: Pass A fails to translate the sense of 'Tenente principium' correctly, rendering it as 'holding the beginning' which is a literalism that obscures the theological meaning of Christ holding the first place/primacy, though Pass B corrects this. However, the primary failure is in Pass A's handling of 'Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo'. Pass A translates this as 'The creature groans, burning with the anger of the highest God', whereas the Latin 'ardet' (burns/is aflame) modifies 'creatura' (the creature burns/is aflame), not the anger. Pass B correctly renders this as 'Creation groans, aflame with the anger of the Most High God'. Pass A also fails the clause 'In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto' by rendering 'acto' as 'done' in a way that lacks syntactic connection to the rest of the sentence, whereas Pass B handles the sense better. Most critically, Pass A's translation of 'Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno' as 'Reward in perpetuity according to deeds to the tyrant' is syntactically ambiguous and potentially reverses the intended meaning compared to the Latin, which implies the reward (or punishment) is given to the tyrant according to his deeds; Pass B's 'Eternal reward goes to the tyrant according to his deeds' is a more faithful rendering of the intended sense.
reasons: Pass A: 'Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo' translated as 'The creature groans, burning with the anger of the highest God' incorrectly attributes the burning to the anger rather than the creature ('ardet creatura').
Pass A: 'Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno' translated as 'Reward in perpetuity according to deeds to the tyrant' is a poor rendering of the Latin syntax compared to Pass B.
